name: 420 Wallet
invariants: WALLET-INV-001: 420 Wallet Web is a replaceable client and never becomes consensus or canonical protocol state authority.
WALLET-INV-002: Wallet Core reuses the canonical Genesis SmartAccount420, SmartAccountFactory420 and CapabilityRegistry420 primitives rather than introducing parallel account authority.
WALLET-INV-003: Account ownership, recovery, capabilities, session policy and revocation remain authoritative at the smart-account/protocol layer and are portable across wallet clients.
WALLET-INV-004: The web client never stores or controls user signing keys on a 420-operated server and never auto-signs transactions.
WALLET-INV-005: Every capability grant, spend approval, high-risk action and transaction execution must pass the canonical wallet/smart-account authorization boundary.

WALLET-INV-006: 420 Search, 420 AppStore, 420 AI, 420 Token and other ecosystem destinations are discovered from canonical Registry data or a signed/versioned ecosystem manifest, not trusted solely because of a URL.

WALLET-INV-007: The final production web-wallet domain may be assigned after implementation; production passkey/WebAuthn relying-party configuration is bound only after that canonical domain is selected.
WALLET-INV-008: Developer Hub, guides, specifications, white papers, SDK/API documentation, contract references and security documentation are first-class wallet navigation targets.
WALLET-INV-009: A compromised, deprecated or revoked ecosystem destination can be marked unsafe without changing the underlying wallet account or protocol authority.
WALLET-INV-010: Browser extension, mobile and desktop clients may later reuse the same Wallet Core account, capability, recovery and session semantics without creating separate identities.
